level_description: Scheduling Regression Confirmation (Not a new-weakness hunt -- this suite is a regression/confirmation artifact. Earlier this project, the field-generation scheduler (dependency_analyzer.cpp) had a bug where a field's own inline constraint referencing a sibling declared LATER in the DSL source could be generated before that sibling existed, silently skipping the check. That was fixed by adding scheduler edges for field-owned validation constraints, not just deterministic-assignment constraints, and confirmed by a synthetic unit test. These two cases reproduce the exact bug shape in realistic, benchmark-style schemas (a 'backwards-declared' field order that a real schema author might plausibly write) to confirm the fix generalizes outside the unit-test harness. Both cases are expected to PASS -- a failure here would indicate the scheduler fix does not hold in practice.

SCH_price_markdown.name: Price Markdown (backwards-declared sibling)
SCH_price_markdown.description: final_price (declared first) has an inline constraint 'value <= this.original_price', but original_price is declared second. Requires the scheduler to generate original_price before final_price despite the declaration order.

prompts.system: You are a retail pricing service generating a validated markdown record. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a markdown pricing record for a clearance item, where the final price is discounted below the original price.

SCH_bonus_plan.name: Bonus Plan (backwards-declared nested sibling)
SCH_bonus_plan.description: bonus_amount (declared first) has an inline constraint referencing 'this.salary_info.base_salary', a field inside a NESTED spec (salary_info) declared second. Tests the scheduler fix combined with multi-segment nested field-path resolution.

prompts.system: You are an HR compensation system generating a validated bonus plan record. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a performance bonus plan for an employee, where the bonus amount is capped relative to their base salary.
